rationale: Although the record concerns sanitation services (C1), it is a macro-level SDG target-mapping study identifying cross-sectoral synergies and trade-offs between sanitation and the 169 UN SDG targets to justify strategic cross-sectoral investment in sanitation. It neither examines a legal, administrative, regulatory, tariff, tenure, or institutional mechanism governing sanitation access (failing C2, E03) nor measures household or community service access as an empirical outcome of such mechanisms (failing C4).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain readings of Criterion 2: the paper is a high-level cross-sectoral mapping of synergies and trade-offs between sanitation investment and the 169 UN Sustainable Development Goal targets, rather than an empirical evaluation of legal, administrative, regulatory, institutional, or governance mechanisms affecting household or community sanitation access.

evidence_quotes.quote: this study identifies linkages between sanitation and each of the 169 Targets on the basis of published evidence.
We show that there are synergies between sanitation and 130 (77%) of the Targets and trade-offs for 28 (17%) of the Targets.
The results demonstrate the far-reaching benefits that can be unlocked from investment in sanitation, which extend beyond health and spread across sectors.
